documents.title: Baby is here
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know the baby came Saturday the 29th, at 39 weeks, regular vaginal delivery, no complications. Everyone is healthy and we're home and very tired. OB has me coming back at 6 weeks. When should I restart the fenofibrate?

documents.title: RE: Baby is here
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Congratulations to all of you! So glad it went smoothly.

Let's hold the fenofibrate until around your six-week mark. Book a visit with me for early to mid January and we'll check fasting lipids and restart it then. Front desk will reach out to schedule.

events.reason: Epigastric pain radiating to the back

conditions.label: Other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY, General Surgery (received by fax 02/13/2026)
Admitted 12/30/2025. Discharged 02/12/2026.

Principal diagnosis: acute necrotizing pancreatitis due to hypertriglyceridemia, complicated by infected pancreatic necrosis.
Secondary: septic shock (resolved); severe hypertriglyceridemia; recurrent UTI; postpartum, delivered 11/29/2025.

Presentation: 29 yo F, about 4 1/2 weeks postpartum, with 24 h of severe, constant epigastric pain boring through to the back and getting worse. Denied nausea, vomiting and fever. Fenofibrate had been stopped for the pregnancy. Vitals stable on arrival. Abdomen soft with epigastric tenderness, no rebound or guarding, bowel sounds normal; no jaundice or scleral icterus.
Labs on admission: Hgb 12.5, WBC 11.0, Plt 250, amylase 450, lipase 600, triglycerides 1,200, calcium 9.2; liver tests within normal limits.
Abdominal ultrasound: no gallstones, no biliary ductal dilatation.

Hospital course:
- Insulin and dextrose infusion for triglycerides; TG 430 on hospital day 3 and infusion stopped. IV fluids, analgesia.
- CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast 01/03 for persistent pain: necrotizing pancreatitis, roughly 30% of the parenchyma in the pancreatic body non-enhancing, acute necrotic collection in the lesser sac.
- 01/20: fever and hypotension, septic shock. Transferred to SICU; norepinephrine for 3 days; meropenem started. CT 01/20: 9 cm walled-off necrotic collection containing gas, consistent with infected necrosis.
- 01/23: EUS-guided transgastric drainage with lumen-apposing metal stent (GI). 01/30: endoscopic necrosectomy x1. Out of the ICU 01/25.
- Meropenem completed, 3 weeks total, in hospital. Afebrile and tolerating a low-fat diet at discharge.

Discharge medications: fenofibrate 145 mg PO daily (resumed).
Diet: low fat.
Follow-up: GI in 3 to 4 weeks with repeat CT for stent removal; PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Home from the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I finally got discharged yesterday. Six weeks. I'm sure you got the paperwork. I need to see you this week if possible, and my school needs a medical leave form from you through at least the end of March. Can I drop it off?

documents.title: RE: Home from the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Welcome home. I have the discharge summary and read it this afternoon. Tuesday at 1:30 is yours. Bring the form or upload it here and I'll fill it out. Our nurse will call you Monday to go over your medicines.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transitional care call, within 2 business days of discharge. Pt at home. Pain mild, using no prescription pain medicine. Eating small low-fat meals, no vomiting, no fevers. Taking fenofibrate daily; no other new medicines. Has GI follow-up being scheduled for early March with CT first. PCP appointment confirmed 2/17 1:30. Reviewed when to call: fever, worsening pain, vomiting, jaundice.

conditions.label: Severe sepsis with septic shock
conditions.note: ICU January 2026, from infected pancreatic necrosis

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here five days after a six-week admission. Discharge summary reviewed in full; RN call yesterday.

In short: hypertriglyceridemia-induced pancreatitis four and a half weeks after delivery, off fenofibrate since the pregnancy, TG 1,200 on arrival. Became necrotizing; the necrosis got infected in week 3 with septic shock and an ICU stay. Endoscopic drainage with a stent through the stomach wall and one necrosectomy. Meropenem finished inside.

Today: worn out but steadier each day. Pain is mild, no medicine for it. Eating five small low-fat meals. No vomiting, no fever. Weight down from where we'd expect after delivery. Stools normal. Taking fenofibrate since discharge. Mood okay. PHQ-9 5.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet, afebrile. Thin, tired-appearing. Sclerae anicteric. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, mild epigastric tenderness, no guarding, no mass. No edema.

A/P
- Infected necrotizing pancreatitis, recovering, stent in place. GI follow-up with CT in early March for stent removal. Call us for fever, worse pain, vomiting or yellowing.
- Severe hypertriglyceridemia: back on fenofibrate 145 mg. Lipids, CMP, CBC, lipase and A1c today. Strict low-fat diet, no alcohol (doesn't drink).
- Septic shock this admission, resolved.
- Postpartum. Screening okay today; we'll keep asking.
- School medical leave form completed through 3/31.

Recheck in about 8 weeks.

documents.title: Labs and your form
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Jasmine, your blood count, kidney and liver tests, lipase and A1c are all normal, which is reassuring after everything. Triglycerides are 690. Expected this soon after restarting fenofibrate and well down from 1,200; we want them to keep coming down, so stay with the low-fat plan. Recheck at your April visit.

Your leave form is done and uploaded to your documents; a copy went to your school's HR fax as you asked.

documents.title: Medical Leave Certification
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:

Jasmine Norris is under my care and is medically unable to work from 12/30/2025 through 03/31/2026 because of a serious illness requiring hospitalization and recovery. I expect her to be able to return to full duties after that date and will update you if that changes.

Primary care physician

documents.title: Stent is out
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Update: CT last Wednesday showed the collection almost gone, about 2 cm left. They took the stent out yesterday with the scope. GI says I'm done with them unless something comes up. Feeling pretty good!

documents.title: RE: Stent is out
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great news. I'll keep an eye out for their report. See you in April.

documents.title: Return to work
documents.author: patient
documents.body: School wants a note saying I can come back April 1. I'd like to start with a lighter schedule the first week if you think that's okay.

documents.title: Return to Work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
To whom it may concern:

Jasmine Norris may return to work on 04/01/2026. I recommend a reduced teaching load for the first week, then full duties without restriction.

Primary care physician

conditions.label: Other acute pancreatitis with infected necrosis

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. Went back to teaching 4/1, half load the first week. No abdominal pain in a month, eating normally on a low-fat pattern, gaining weight back. GI removed the transgastric stent 3/11 after CT 3/4 showed a 2.1 cm residual; their note still hasn't come, but her account is clear. On fenofibrate daily.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Looks well. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
- Infected necrotizing pancreatitis: resolved clinically, off GI follow-up. Moving it to resolved on the problem list.
- History of septic shock, January 2026.
- Hypertriglyceridemia: fenofibrate 145 mg, low-fat diet. Lipids today. Talked through the obvious lesson: if there is another pregnancy, we plan the triglycerides with OB from the start.

Annual in August.
